_comment: Voice-over, one entry per video segment. {placeholders} are filled from docs/slides/deck_data.json.
title: Table for Two. Two robot arms set a dinner table from a single sentence, planned and driven on Intel OpenVINO.
plan: A small language model, running locally on OpenVINO, turns the instruction into a step-by-step plan. Before the robot moves, every plan is checked: the planner simulates what each hand is holding, so the arms never pour without the bottle.
demo: Nothing here is glued to a gripper. Every object moves only because the fingers squeeze it and friction holds it. The learned policy runs the plate, the drawer and mug, the fork and the bottle pick-up, and the scripted skills do the stages it cannot yet do reliably; each stage is labelled on screen. Both arms pinch the plate from opposite sides and carry it level to the placemat, and every object is lowered until it touches the table before the fingers let go. The left arm pulls the drawer open by its handle while the right arm sets the mug down, and the fork goes beside the plate. The right arm grips the bottle from the side, tilts it over the mug, and the water, twenty-four small beads, pours in. Then the left arm turns the spoon and hands it across to the right.
grid: Robustness matters. Across ten randomised scenes we change object positions, masses, friction, lighting and the colour of the table, so a grasp that is too weak really does drop the object.
results: On the same ten scenes, the learned policy carries the plate, opens the drawer and places the mug every time, and lays the fork in nine. The pour, the bottle return and the hand-over still break the chain, so it has not yet set a whole table on its own. Started cleanly, it puts the bottle back ten times out of ten and hands the spoon over in five, and most of the water lands in the mug, with a few beads too many spilled. We report its weak spots as they are.
latency: On Intel hardware, NNCF INT8 quantisation runs the policy in {int8_cpu_ms} milliseconds on the CPU, {int8_speedup_words} faster than full precision.
closing: Grasps are real contact, stages finished by a script are never counted as policy wins, and everything you have seen is reproducible from our repository. Thank you.
